questions.q:
An element undergoes a reaction as shown :

$\text{X} + 2 {\text{e}}^{-} \to {\text{X}}^{2 -}$, energy released $= 30 .87 eV / atom$. If the energy released is used to dissociate $4gms$ of ${H}_{2}$ molecules, equally into ${H}^{+}$ and ${H}^{*}$, where ${H}^{*}$ is excited state of $H$ atoms where the electron travels in orbit whose circumference equal to four times its de Broglie's wavelength. Determine the least moles of $X$ that would be required:

Given: I.E. of $H = 13 .6 eV / atom$ bond energy of ${H}_{2} = 4 .526 eV / molecule$.
questions.solution:
Total energy requirement per molecule of ${H}_{2}$:

Binding energy $\text{=4}\text{.526 eV}$

$\text{I}\text{.E}\text{=}\text{13}\text{.60}\text{eV}$

According to de Broglie's explanation of Bohr's orbit-

${\text{2 \pi r}}_{n} = \text{n \lambda}$

As per question, $\text{2 \pi r} = \text{4 \lambda}$

Thus, electron is excited to the 4th Bohr orbit

Excitation energy~$= {E}_{4} - {E}_{1} = - 0 .85 - \left(- 13 .60\right) = 12 .75 eV$~

Thus, total eenergy requirement per molecule $= 13 .60 + 12 .75 + 4 .526 ≅ 30 .87 eV$

Thus, $\text{1}$ molecule of ${H}_{2}$ will be dissociated by $\text{1}$ atom of $\text{X}$

Therefore, $\left(4{gH}_{2}\right) ≡ 2$~moles of ${H}_{2}$ molecules will be dissociated by $2$ moles of $X$.

questions.q: A light of wavelength $3000\overset{o}{\text{A}}$ falls on a metal surface. Ejected ${e}^{-}$ is further accelerated by a potential difference of $2V$ , then final K.E of the ${e}^{-}$ is found to be $8 \times 1{0}^{- 19}J$ . If threshold energy for the metal surface is $\text{'}{\text{ϕ}}^{'}eV$ . Then find the numerical value of $8ϕ$
questions.solution:
${\text{KE}}_{\text{final}} \text{=}{\text{E}}_{\text{photon}} \text{+}{\text{E}}_{\text{potential}} - ϕ$
where $ϕ$ = threshold energy for metal surface
${\text{E}}_{\text{photon}} \text{=}\dfrac{\text{hc}}{\text{\lambda}} = \dfrac{6.6 \times {10}^{- 34} \times 3 \times {10}^{8}}{3000 \times {10}^{- 10}}$
$≃ 6.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \text{J} = 4.12\text{eV}$
${\text{E}}_{\text{potential}} \text{=}\text{2}\text{eV}$
${\text{KE}}_{\text{final}} = \dfrac{8 \times {10}^{- 19} \text{J}}{1.6 \times {10}^{- 19} \text{J}} = 5\text{eV}$
Hence, $ϕ = ( 4.12 + 2 - 5 ) \text{eV} = 1.125\text{eV}$
Numerical value = $8 \times 1.125 = 9$
